The #266/#267 fix gives `MProvView` a shared way to serve details: `GET /<endpoint>/<pk>/` and `GET /<endpoint>/?detail` use `detail_serializer_class`, or a depth-3 subclass of `serializer_class` when a view doesn't set one.

Three views have their own `get()` and never reach that code:

- `JobAPIView` (`jobqueue/views.py`)

mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#112: job servers claim jobs by GETting `jobs/?search=<module>` and PATCHing every unfinished job to `jobserver=<self>`. Two job servers running the same module both claim the same jobs, and whichever PATCHes last wins.

The mPCC has no way to arbitrate this today: `PATCH /jobs/<id>/` always succeeds.

**Proposed:** a claim operation the mPCC makes atomic, e.g. `POST /jobs/<id>/claim/` (or `POST /jobs/claim/?module=<module>`, returning the next pending job). It sets `jobserver` and status "running" only if the job is still pending and unassigned, using `Job.objects.filter(pk=…, status=pending, jobserver=None).update(…)` and checking the row count. It returns 200 with the job if the claim succeeded, or 409 if another job server got it first.

**Coordinate with:**
- mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#112 (the jobserver switches to the claim call).
- #254 (network-aware routing should also decide which job server may claim a job).
- mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#94 (failing a restarted server's running jobs).

Tests: two claims on the same pending job, where only the first succeeds; a claim on a running or finished job returns 409.

About half of the mPCC models use a slug as their primary key (`SystemImage`, `SystemModel`, `SystemLocation`, `OSType`, `DiskLayout`, `JobModule`, `Script`, `File`, the Ansible models). The rest use Django's integer `id`, including `System`, `SystemGroup`, `OSDistro`, `OSRepo`, `JobServer`, `Switch`, `SystemBMC` and `NetworkInterface`. `Network` and `NetworkType` have a unique slug but still use an integer primary key.

As a result, the API mixes the two. Clients get numeric IDs for some relations (`systems/` returns `systemgroups` as `[10, 11]`, `systemimages/` returns `osdistro` as `1`) and slugs for others, and they have to look up names themselves to write anything human-readable. mprov_jobserver's libgenders wrote group names into `/etc/genders` without slugifying them, and a group named `A100 MIG 3 x 20G` broke the file's syntax (mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#117).

**Proposal:** give every model that people name a slug primary key, or at least a unique slug that the API uses for lookups and relations. Purely internal records (`Job`, `JobStatus`, `DiskPartition`, `SwitchPort`) can stay numeric.

**Considerations:**
- Changing a primary key needs data migrations for every foreign key and many-to-many table that points at the model. Plan these model by model, with a tested way back.
- This changes the API contract. mprov_jobserver, mprov_scripts, mash and mprov_boot all reference these IDs, so each client needs updating in step, or the API has to accept both forms for a while.
- Decide how a slug changes when the name changes. Slug primary keys today are mostly `editable=False`.

Related: mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#117, #266.

The jobserver image is built on `rockylinux/rockylinux:8.8` with Python 3.8 (`Dockerfile`; `Containerfile` is a symlink to it). Move it to the latest Rocky Linux 9 with a current Python. The same change for the mPCC is mprov-ng/mprov_control_center#197.

## Why

- **Python 3.8 has been end-of-life since October 2024.** It no longer gets security fixes, and CI (`ci_build.yml`) still builds and tests the package with Python 3.8.
- **The image installs two Pythons.** It installs both `python38*` and `python3.11-pip`/`python3.11-devel`, then runs a plain `pip3 install`. Which interpreter the jobserver ends up on depends on what `pip3` and `python3` resolve to. It should have one Python.
- **The base image is pinned to 8.8, but the build installs 8.10 packages anyway.** `dnf update` pulls everything up to 8.10, so the pin doesn't hold anything back.

## The jobserver's OS matters more than the mPCC's

The jobserver builds node images (`dnf --installroot ... --releasever=<distro version>` in `image_update_mod/rhel.py`) and syncs repos (`dnf reposync` in `repo_update_mod/rhel.py`) with its own dnf and rpm. So its OS version affects the output:

- #97: Rocky 9 images didn't build right on a Rocky 8 host, so an `rpm --rebuilddb` workaround is in place until #92 (cloud images as the base) is done.
- #80: creating a Rocky 8 repo on a Rocky 9 jobserver failed on GPG keys.

Before switching, test both directions on a Rocky 9 jobserver: build Rocky 8 and Rocky 9 images, and sync Rocky 8 and Rocky 9 repos. Check whether the #97 `rebuilddb` workaround is still needed, or becomes needed for EL8 images instead. Doing #92 first, or at the same time, would remove most of this host dependency.

## What changes

In the `Dockerfile`:
- The base image becomes `rockylinux/rockylinux:9` (or a pinned 9.x).
- PowerTools is called CRB on EL9: `dnf config-manager --enable crb`.
- Use one Python (3.11 or 3.12 from AppStream) and remove `python38*`. Use that interpreter's pip explicitly, for example `python3.11 -m pip install`.
- Check the rest of the package list on EL9: `dnsmasq`, `ipmitool`, `tcpdump`, `parted-devel` and the "Development Tools" group.
- The plugin copy path `/usr/local/lib/python3.*/site-packages/...` should still match, but confirm it only matches one Python.

In Python dependencies:
- Check that `requirements.txt` builds on the new Python. The pinned `pyparted==3.11.7` (which needs `parted-devel`) and `pyroute2==0.8.1` matter most, along with `py-dmidecode` and `netifaces`.
- Update `setup.cfg`: `python_requires` and the classifiers still list 3.8.

In CI:
- `ci_build.yml` uses `actions/setup-python@v3` with Python 3.8. Move it to the new Python version and a current major of the action.

## Done when

- The image builds on Rocky 9, CI builds and tests on the new Python, and the image has only one Python.
- A Rocky 9 jobserver deployed through mprov-compose can build Rocky 8 and Rocky 9 images, sync Rocky 8 and Rocky 9 repos, and serve PXE/DHCP (dnsmasq) for a node boot.
- The README and docs no longer say Rocky 8 or Python 3.8.

`JobServer.update_job_status()` in `app.py`, called without `jobid` or `jobquery`, fetches `jobs/?search=<module>`. That's every job of the module, any status and any job server. It then PATCHes each one that isn't finished to the new status with `jobserver=<self>`. So:
- Every job server running a module claims all of that module's pending jobs at once, and can take over a job another server has already marked running; whichever PATCHes last wins `jobserver`.
- Finished jobs are skipped, but the GET still returns the module's whole job history each poll, so the poll grows with the job table.

`plugins/repo_update.py` then lists `jobs/?jobserver=<self>&module=<module>&status=2`, so two job servers can both sync the same repo, or a job can end up assigned to a server that isn't running it.

**Suggested fix:** when claiming, query only pending jobs (`jobs/?module=<module>&status=1`), and claim one job at a time in a way the mPCC can arbitrate. For example, a claim endpoint that atomically sets `jobserver` only if it's still null, or a conditional PATCH that the mPCC rejects when the job is no longer pending.

Related: `plugins/image_update.py` passes `jobquery='{"imageId": "<image>"}'`, which requests `jobs/?{"imageId": ...}`, a bare query key the mPCC ignores. So that filter matches every job too (mPCC review item D-62). Once mprov-ng/mprov_control_center#244 merges, `jobs/?params={"imageId":"<image>"}` works.

A job server can serve more than one network, but it registers with the mPCC once: through its single `mprovURL`, with the address of its socket to that URL (or `myaddress` from config) and its hostname as its name. So the mPCC only knows it on one network.

**Proposed:**

- Let the job server register on every network it serves: either a list of mPCC URLs, one per network (it connects to each and registers through it), or one URL plus a list of addresses/networks to register under.
- Send the same stable host id with every registration (see #113), so the mPCC can tell these are one host seen on several networks.
- Heartbeat each registration, so the mPCC can tell which networks the server is reachable on.

The mPCC side (one registration per host id and network, recording the address each registration came from, and routing requests to a job server on the requester's network) is tracked in mprov-ng/mprov_control_center#254.

History: #62 (report itself for all interfaces) was closed in 2022 in favour of #61 (register by hostname and rely on mPCC-managed DNS). Per-network routing, busy servers and reboots now depend on identity, so this revisits that.

Related: #112, #113.

`app.py` makes sure `mprovURL` ends with `/` when it loads the config, but several plugins then add a path that starts with `/`, so the URL has `//` after the host:

- `plugins/nads.py`: `query = '/systems/register'`, posted to `f"{self.js.mprovURL}{query}"` → `http://mpcc//systems/register`
- `plugins/repo_update_mod/rhel.py:22`: `f"{self.js.mprovURL}/ostypes/"`
- `plugins/image_update_mod/rhel.py:25`: `f"{self.js.mprovURL}/ostypes/"`
- `plugins/image_update_mod/rhel.py:64` and `:132`: `f"{self.js.mprovURL}/osrepos/..."`, which ends up as the dnf `baseurl` in built images

These only work because Apache merges duplicate slashes by default (`MergeSlashes On`, httpd 2.4.39+). Behind a server or proxy that doesn't, or Django's own server, Django sees a path starting with `/` and returns 404: N.A.D.S. registration fails, and image builds can't reach their repos.

**Fix:** drop the leading `/` from those paths (`'systems/register'`, `f"{self.js.mprovURL}ostypes/"`, `f"{self.js.mprovURL}osrepos/..."`), matching the other plugins, which already write `self.js.mprovURL + 'jobs/...'`.

Found while reviewing mprov-ng/mprov_control_center#216.

mprov_jobserver has no tests. Plugin bugs have only shown up in production:
- libgenders wrote unparsable genders files (#117, #118);
- the dnsmasq DHCP plugin tagged hosts with the wrong value and never merged switches (#119).

The checks for both fixes were one-off scratch scripts. They ran each plugin's `handle_jobs()` in a container against stubbed mPCC responses and checked the files it wrote (`dnsmasq --test` for the DHCP output). The same approach would work as a permanent suite.

## Proposal
- A `tests/` directory using pytest, with a fake `session` that serves canned mPCC responses by URL. That includes the awkward ones: `404` with `null`, lists with nested or flat relations, empty lists.
- Plugins write to a temporary directory: `/etc/genders`, the dnsmasq conf dir, image and repo dirs. Process handling (`psutil`, `os.kill`, `os.system`, `chroot`) is stubbed out.
- Assertions on the generated output. Where there's a validator, run it too: `nodeattr -k` for genders, `dnsmasq --test` for the dnsmasq configs.
- Run the suite on pull requests in CI. The PR workflows from #123 are the natural place.

## Plugins
`libgenders`, `dnsmasq` (`dnsmasq_mod/config.py`, `dhcp.py`, `dns.py`), `image_sync`, `image_update` (+ `image_update_mod/rhel.py`), `image_delete`, `repo_sync`, `repo_update` (+ `repo_update_mod/rhel.py`), `repo_delete`, `script_runner`, `nads`, `mprov_webserver`, and the job handling in `plugin.py` and `app.py`.

Suggested order: libgenders and dnsmasq first (pure file generation, and the scratch checks already exist), then the job-state handling in `plugin.py`/`app.py`, then the image and repo plugins, which need the most stubbing.

## Things to sort out
- `plugins/__init__.py` imports every plugin (`from . import *`), so importing any one of them pulls in `pyparted`, `pyroute2`, `netifaces` and the rest. The suite either installs the full requirements (`pyparted` needs `libparted-dev`) or the import should become lazy.
- Templates are loaded with `PackageLoader("mprov_jobserver")`, so the package has to be installed, or the loader swapped in tests.

Related: #117, #119, #123.

`plugins/image_update.py` applies the OS distro's `rootsshkeys` and `rootpw` to an image before running its image-gen scripts ([lines 334-348](https://github.com/mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver/blob/8b17093/src/mprov_jobserver/plugins/image_update.py#L334-L348)). Both have bugs.

**1. SSH keys: the directory is created on the job server, not in the image.**

```python
os.makedirs("/root/.ssh", exist_ok=True)
with open(imgDir + '/root/.ssh/authorized_keys', mode="w") as authkeys:
```

`makedirs` creates `/root/.ssh` on the job server host. If the image has no `/root/.ssh`, which is normal for a freshly built image, the `open()` fails and only `WARN: No authorized_keys copied, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys access error` is printed. The image gets no root keys.

Fix: `os.makedirs(imgDir + "/root/.ssh", mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)`, write `authorized_keys` with mode `0600`, and make sure it ends with a newline.

**2. Password: passed through `echo -e` in a shell command.**

```python
os.system(f"echo -e '{rootpw}\n{rootpw}' | chroot {imgDir} passwd root")
```

This works for simple passwords. I tested it on Rocky 9: `passwd` accepts the piped input. But:
- A password containing `'` breaks the shell quoting, and `passwd` fails with `Authentication token manipulation error`. Only the `passwd` output is printed, and the build carries on.
- `echo -e` turns `\t`, `\n` and similar sequences in the password into control characters, so the password that gets set differs from the one in the distro, without any error.
- The password ends up on a shell command line, where it shows up in the process list.

Fix: run `chpasswd` without a shell, for example `subprocess.run(["chroot", imgDir, "chpasswd"], input=f"root:{rootpw}\n", text=True, check=False)`. Log the result. If the field is meant to be able to hold a hash, use `chpasswd -e` for values starting with `$`.

**Also related:** image-gen scripts that still read `rootpw`/`rootsshkey` from config params ran *after* this code, and replaced the distro's settings with `null` when those params weren't set. That's fixed in mprov-ng/mprov_scripts#18 (#16 there).

**Possibly explains:** mprov-ng/mprov_control_center#148 ("root pw not set on new image generation") and #149 ("Root ssh key not reading from Distro config").

Tests: this would fit in the plugin test suite planned in #125. Pass `image_update` a temporary `imgDir` with no `/root/.ssh`, then check `authorized_keys`; and check that the `chpasswd` input is built correctly for a password containing `'` and `\`.

Moved from review item D-67 in `REVIEW-2026-10.md`. Found while reviewing #243 (D-52).

## Problem

Job servers are deleted automatically once their heartbeat is over a minute old (`JobServer.save()`, made reliable by #243). But a busy job server deliberately stops heartbeating, and a rebooting one stops too. Deleting it:

- sets `jobserver` to null on its jobs, including the ones it's running;
- drops it from every image's `jobservers` and every repo's `hosted_by`;
- queues a repo-update job for every repo (`DeleteJobserver`);
- and it comes back as a new row with a new id.

The mPCC also only knows a job server on one network: `JobServer.name` is unique, the `network` field is never set (the auto-detect in `save()` is commented out and `POST /jobservers/` ignores it), and the address is whatever the job server sends. Requests aren't routed by network: `/images/` picks the least-loaded job server hosting the image (only choosing A vs AAAA by the client's IP family), and `/osrepos/` picks one at random.

## Proposed

- **Identity:** a job server host sends a stable host id (e.g. `/etc/machine-id`). The host id isn't unique per row: the mPCC keeps one registration per host id and network it sees that host on, each with the network, the address, a heartbeat and a busy state. `JobServer.name` stops being unique.
- **Address and network from the request:** record the address a registration came in from (`REMOTE_ADDR` / `X-Forwarded-For`), work out which `Network` it falls in, and store both, instead of trusting the address the job server sends.
- **Network-aware routing:** when picking a job server for `/images/`, `/osrepos/` and job claiming (mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#112), choose among registrations on the requester's network, then by load, skipping unresponsive and busy ones. `/osrepos/` should pick the least-loaded server, not a random one (review item D-66).
- **Flag, don't delete:** a registration whose heartbeat is old is flagged unresponsive and left out of selection, not deleted. Deleting a job server becomes a manual admin action. This replaces the automatic delete in `JobServer.save()` (D-52) and the `DeleteJobserver` repo-update jobs.

## Job server side

- mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#113: keep heartbeating under load and report busy, and send the host id.
- mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#114: register on every network the job server serves.
- mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#112: job servers claim every job of a module.
- History: mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#62 (report itself on all interfaces) was closed in 2022 in favour of mprov-ng/mprov_jobserver#61 (register by hostname and rely on mPCC-managed DNS).

Since #232 (review item D-35), `/jobqueue/status-changes/` returns 403 unless the user is an active staff member. The admin's job toast script (`jobqueue/static/admin/js/job_notifications.js`) polls it every second and never checks the status, so:

- when the admin session times out on an open page, the toasts stop silently and the page keeps polling every second;
- the script also loads on the admin login page (it's in `templates/admin/base.html`), so it polls there too and gets a 403 every second.

**Proposed:**

1. Only load the toast script for logged-in staff: wrap its tags in `templates/admin/base.html` in `{% if request.user.is_active and request.user.is_staff %}`. The login page and other logged-out pages then don't poll at all.
2. In `pollJobStatusChanges()`, if the response is 403 (or a redirect to the login page), stop the `setInterval` and send the user to `/admin/login/?next=<current path and query>`, so they log in again and land back where they were.

Part 1 has to come with part 2: without it, the login page would get the 403 and redirect to itself forever.

Add a test that the toast script isn't on the login page, and that it is on an admin page for a staff user.

content.body:
Job modules should only be created by job servers, when they register. Today nothing does that:

- `JobServersAPIView.post` (`POST /jobservers/`) looks each advertised module up with `JobModule.objects.get(pk=...)` and returns 500 ("Error locating jobmodule") for one it doesn't know, so a job server can't register a new module.
- `JobModule.slug` is the primary key and `editable=False`, and `JobModule` has no `save()` that makes one, so `POST /jobmodules/` creates a module with an empty ID (review item D-59).
- `JobModuleAdmin.has_add_permission()` returns True only when the URL contains "add" or "change", which hides the Add button but leaves `/admin/jobqueue/jobmodule/add/` working; that form can't set the ID either, so it also saves an empty ID (D-63).

All the module IDs in use today come from the `jobqueue` fixture.

**Proposed:**

- `POST /jobservers/`: for each module the job server advertises, `JobModule.objects.get_or_create(slug=<id>, defaults={"name": <id>})` instead of returning 500. Admins can rename a module afterwards.
- `POST /jobmodules/` returns 405. `PATCH` can still change `name`, not the ID.
- `JobModuleAdmin.has_add_permission()` returns False, which also closes the `/add/` URL. Editing stays allowed.
- Tests: a job server registering an unknown module creates it and registers; POST `/jobmodules/` is 405; the admin add page is 403.

A typo in a job server's config would create a stray module; the fixture still loads the standard ones.

Replaces #245 (D-59), closed unmerged, and review item D-63.

content.body:
In `common/views.py`:

```python
def delete(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    ...
    return self.destroy(request, args, kwargs)        # line 174

def patch(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    ...
    return self.partial_update(request, args, kwargs)  # line 183
```

`args` and `kwargs` are passed as two positional arguments (a tuple and a dict) instead of `*args, **kwargs`. It works today only because DRF's `get_object()` reads the primary key from `self.kwargs` and ignores the method arguments. It's the same kind of bug as D-03 (#206), where `retrieve()` was passed `self` as the request. `post()` at line 171 already unpacks them correctly.

**Fix:** `return self.destroy(request, *args, **kwargs)` and `return self.partial_update(request, *args, **kwargs)`. No behaviour should change, so no API client is affected. The PATCH and DELETE tests should still pass.

Found while reviewing #257.

content.body:
There are three implementations of the distro → system groups → system config inheritance, and they disagree:

- [`systems/models.py:124`](https://github.com/mprov-ng/mprov_control_center/blob/e36525c65c6aa2202df8ec749cb9dea3990c7581/systems/models.py#L124) `System.flatten_config` is the only live one. It feeds `System.config`, which `SystemSerializer` and `SystemDetailSerializer` expose to nodes. `install_kernel_cmdline` and `initial_mods` append, and a leading `=` overwrites. Other fields overwrite when they're non-empty or non-zero. `config_params` is replaced as a whole string, with no YAML key merge.
- [`common/__init__.py:50`](https://github.com/mprov-ng/mprov_control_center/blob/e36525c65c6aa2202df8ec749cb9dea3990c7581/common/__init__.py#L50) `render_config` is never called. It overwrites every field, including the cmdline and module list, and has no `=` handling. `params` is YAML-parsed but still replaced whole. It collects ansible playbooks, roles, collections and scripts with a `source` per layer, which `flatten_config` doesn't do. Bugs: a group's `tmpfs_root_size` is checked with `!= ""`, so a group `0` overrides the distro. Its only intended consumer, `systems/templates/admin/rendered_config.html`, is unreferenced; the admin code that used it is on the unmerged branch `origin/rendered_config` (`9d89e0f`).
- [`common/__init__.py:5`](https://github.com/mprov-ng/mprov_control_center/blob/e36525c65c6aa2202df8ec749cb9dea3990c7581/common/__init__.py#L5) `parse_config_params` is never called. It's the only one that merges `config_params` YAML by key. It iterates `params_obj.systemgroups` without `.all()`, so it would fail on a related manager.

**Decide:**
1. Whether `config_params` should be key-merged across layers, or keep last-layer-wins.
2. Whether to keep one implementation (probably `flatten_config`, extended with the YAML merge and source tracking if wanted) and delete the others.
3. Whether the admin "rendered config" view is worth reviving. If it is, build it on the implementation that's kept. If not, delete `rendered_config.html`, the `is_list` filter in `systems/templatetags/custom_filters.py`, `render_config` and the `origin/rendered_config` branch together.

**Check first:** what `mprov_jobserver` does with `config['config_params']` and with the ansible and script lists; some merging may happen there. Extend `systems/tests.py` to pin down whatever is decided.

Closes #172.

The version box already rendered as `<input type="number">`, so the cause isn't a missing `NumberInput`. It's the input's `min`: `version` is a `BigIntegerField`, so Django sets `min=-9223372036854775808`. A number input counts its steps from `min`, and browsers do that in floating point, which can't land on value + 1 from that base, so the arrows left the value unchanged. Checked in headless Chrome: `stepUp()` from 1 stays at 1 with Django's `min`, and goes to 2 with `min=0` or `min=1`. The 2^63 `max` makes no difference.

**Fix:** a shared `VERSION_OVERRIDES` (`formfield_overrides`, `min_value: 1`) on the five scripts admins (Script, File, AnsiblePlaybook, AnsibleRole, AnsibleCollection). The input now has `min="1"`, and the admin form rejects a version below 1.

Admin only: no migration and no API change, so the jobserver, mprov_scripts and mash are unaffected.

**Tests:** `scripts/test_version_widget.py` checks `min` is 1 on all five admin forms. It fails on `main` and passes here. The full suite (158 tests) passes in the Docker image. Closes #129.

`UpdateImage.handle_jobs()` ran `os.chdir(imgDir)` and never changed back. Plugins are threads of one process, so this moved every other plugin's working directory, and left the whole jobserver in the last image's directory until restart (and in a deleted directory if `image_delete` then removed that image). It races with the relative paths in repo_update (#130) and repo_sync (#131).

**Fix:** removes the `chdir`, with a comment. Nothing depends on it:
- every path after it in `rhel.py` is absolute (`--installroot={imgDir}`, `chroot {imgDir}`, `{imgDir}/etc/yum.repos.d/...`); the host `dnf -y clean all` doesn't use the cwd; the relative `wget -O {file}` of the repo RPM is commented out
- the post-build steps in `image_update.py` use `imgDir` or `/tmp` paths
- `script-runner.sh` chroots into a new process, whose `!include plugins/*.yaml` resolves relative to the config file
- `imageDir` is `/export/images` (absolute), and `rhel` is the only `image_update_mod` module

**Tested:** in `ghcr.io/mprov-ng/mprov-jobserver:dev` with the changed `rhel.py` in place: the module imports, and `handle_jobs()` runs start to end with `os.system`/`shutil.copyfile` stubbed out. All 24 commands use absolute `imgDir` paths, the repo file is written under `imgDir`, and the cwd stays `/`. No real image build (that comes with #128's testing). content.body:
Closes #160. Replaces #166, which conflicted with main and was 312 commits behind. Its one new commit is cherry-picked here as `606c818`, with the original author kept and its migration renamed to `0070`.

## What changes

- **`System.provision`**: on means the next PXE boot provisions the system. iPXE netboots only when the requesting NIC is **bootable** and the system has **provision** set. N.A.D.S. boots always netboot. Requiring the bootable NIC as well stops already-installed stateful systems from being reinstalled.
- **One bootable NIC per system:** `bootable` now means "the NIC this system PXE boots from". Saving a NIC as bootable clears the flag on the system's other NICs, and the admin NIC inline rejects two.
- **Migration `0071`** (data): existing systems get `provision = has a bootable NIC`. Systems with several bootable NICs keep one: the NIC named in `prov_interface`, otherwise the oldest.
- **`POST /systems/?self`** (the stateful installer): `{"netboot": false}` clears `provision` and leaves the boot NIC alone. `{"netboot": true}` sets `provision` and makes the requesting NIC the bootable one. This covers the change-form buttons, `/power/pxe/` and `/power/pxeefi/` by `?id=`, `?hostname=` (mash `bmc power`) or a BMC filter, and the "Boot to PXE" admin actions. The buttons now show the error text.

- `static/mprov_stateful.py` sends `{"netboot": false}` and only checks for a 200, so it works unchanged. Only its header comment is updated.
- mash `bmc power` ignores the reply.
- The jobserver doesn't read `bootable`, and doesn't call `?self` POST or `/power/`.
- `mprov_scripts` `tools/add_systems.mash` and `import_systems_csv.sh` create NICs with `bootable=1`, which still picks the boot NIC.

The client code needs checking against these changes before merge.

The full suite passes in the CI image (192 tests, `manage.py check` clean, migrations check included). New tests are in `systems/test_provision.py`:

- `?self` with false/true/strings/bad values/other keys/unknown IP/anonymous, plus the installer's full flow.

`systems/test_bulk_update.py` now tests `provision` instead of `set_bootable`.

`UpdateRepo.handle_jobs()` ran `os.chdir(repoDir)` and then `dnf reposync ... --destdir=./`. Plugins are threads of one process, so the `chdir` moved every other plugin's working directory, and another plugin's `chdir` between the two lines could send the reposync into its directory (e.g. inside an image tree).

**Fix:** drop the `chdir` and pass `--destdir={repoDir}/`. In the image's `dnf-plugins-core` 4.0.21, reposync writes to `realpath(join(cwd, destdir, repo_id))`; an absolute `destdir` replaces the cwd, and `--installroot` doesn't change it. So repos still land in `{repoDir}/{id}`. The rest of `UpdateRepo` already uses absolute paths.

**Tests:** `tests/test_repo_update.py`: the reposync command has an absolute `--destdir` and no `./`, the cwd is unchanged, the repo is PATCHed as `hosted_by` this jobserver and the job marked done; a failing reposync fails the job without a PATCH. The fake session gains `patch()`. 14 passed; with the old `rhel.py` the first test fails. No real reposync was run.

## Covered
- **`plugin.py`:** config loading (defaults, unknown entries, empty sections), `run()`, job states, `checkHTTPStatus()`.
- **`app.py`:**
  - `update_job_status()`: which jobs it updates, URLs, payloads, errors.
  - `register_server()`: payload and port; the double-encoded reply (mprov_control_center#268); 400/500 replies.
  - `load_config()`, including `!include` and the URL slash; `-m`; `startSession()`; the runonce loop.
- **`image_delete`, `image_sync`.**
- **`image_update` + `image_update_mod/rhel.py`:**
  - Hosting images from other job servers.
  - A full build: repo files, dnf, the script-runner config, packing and registration. Commands are recorded, not run.
  - Waiting on repo-update jobs, failure paths, and the dnf fallbacks.
- **`repo_update` + `repo_update_mod/rhel.py`, `repo_sync`, `repo_delete`.** These are added to the per-plugin files from #140 (`test_repo_update.py`) and #150 (`test_repo_sync.py`), without repeating the tests those already have; `repo_delete` has its own file.
- **`script_runner`:** `depResolve()`, dependency order, the `entity.json` config merge and API key, `-i`/`-s`/`-b`, the N.A.D.S. fallback, arguments.
- **`nads`:** LLDP parsing from crafted frames, registration, reboot.
- **`mprov_webserver`:** a real server on localhost.

`conftest.py`: the fake session now:
- records POSTs and PATCHes in `writes`. PATCHes also go in `patches`, as #140 added; this branch merges `main`.
- serves file downloads (`bytes` routes).
- carries `headers`.

A new `commands` fixture records `os.system` calls.

## Bugs found
Each one is a `strict` xfail, so its test starts passing (and the xfail has to be removed) when it's fixed:

- #141: `image_sync`/`repo_sync` crash on an image or repo deleted from the mPCC.
- #142: `image_update` doesn't host images pulled from other job servers.
- #143: a failed `image_update` build fails every running job on the job server.
- #144: other `image_update` error-path bugs.
- #145: `repo_update`'s error paths crash.
- #146: `script_runner` crashes on scripts with dependencies.
- #147: `loadmon` is read from `config_data` (KeyError/AttributeError under load).
- #148: `mprov_webserver`'s per-image connection limit never applies.
- #149: `nads` registers `None` without LLDP, and keeps the Port ID subtype byte.

Also, not opened as an issue: `repo_delete` is still the base plugin. It marks the mPCC's "Delete Repos" jobs done after the base class's simulated 15 seconds and deletes nothing. The test pins that.

The mPCC double-encodes its `POST /jobservers/` reply: the body is a JSON string that holds the JSON object. mprov-ng/mprov_control_center#268 will change it to return the object itself. `register_server()` in `app.py` only understands the double-encoded form:

symptom: A .mash script executes arbitrary Python with the invoking user's full
permissions while reading as a plain command script: every command line, foreach
body and backtick expression renders as a template, invisibly — the API key in the
config is readable from the payload.
evidence: src/mash/app.py:467-473 — renderString builds a plain jinja2
Environment(loader=BaseLoader, autoescape=False) and calls from_string().render();
used by precmd (:648) and do_endforeach (:430). Execution-verified at commit 36b6a5e: a
__class__/__mro__ payload returned 513 reachable subclasses; a __globals__ payload
returned the platform string.
root cause: Untrusted script text treated as a trusted template; Jinja2 is
Turing-complete and walks object graphs unless sandboxed.
proposed fix: Render with jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment (safe filters, no
attribute-walking into unsafe internals) and document that let/foreach only
interpolate variables.
severity: S2 — silent full-privilege execution from the shared script format;
escalates to S1 if mash scripts are ever fetched or executed remotely.
